{{c|''He threateneth the Iewes to be {{ls}}one for{{ls}}aken vnles they doe penance, 10. and confoundeth them for maligning him for his miraculous good doing on the Sabboths. 18. but his kingdom (the Church) as contemptible as it {{ls}}eemeth to them now in the beginning, {{ls}}hal {{ls}}pread ouer al the world, 20. and conuert al, 23. and what an hart{{ls}}ore it {{ls}}hal be to them at the la{{ls}}t day, to {{ls}}ee them {{ls}}elues excluded from the glorie of this kingdom, and the Gentils admitted in their place. 31. foretelling that it is not Galilee that he feareth, but that ob{{ls}}tinate and reprobate Hieru{{ls}}alem vvil nedes murder him, as al{{ls}}o his me{{ls}}{{ls}}engers afore and after him,''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=13|verse=1}}}}ND there vvere certaine pre{{ls}}ent at that very time telling him of the Galilaeans, vvho{{ls}}e bloud Pilate mingled vvith their {{ls}}acrifices. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=2}} And he an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}aid to them, Thinke you that {{sup|‖}} the{{ls}}e Galileans vvere {{ls}}inners more then al the Galilaeans that they {{ls}}uffred {{ls}}uch things? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=3}} No, I {{ls}}ay to you: but vnles you {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Or as it is vttered in other places, ''do penāce, μετανοῆτε''. the which in the new Te{{ls}}tament {{ls}}ignifieth perfect repentance.
